name: Zinc Oxide
metric: E(1%, 1cm) — intrinsic, derived from published mass extinction k(λ) via E1% = k(L/g/cm) x 10. Reflects well-dispersed, ~50 nm primary particles in dilute cuvette measurement.
primary_sources: US20060228310 (Croda) — patent specifying E_max = 12-20 L/g/cm, most preferred 15-16
Patent E360 = 11-20 L/g/cm (most preferred 13.5-14.5), E308 = 11-20 (most preferred 12.5-13.5)
Egerton & Tooley 2012 IJCS 34:117 — Mie theory α(310 nm) ≈ 6-10 L/g/cm, α(360 nm) ≈ 4-7 L/g/cm
Cole, Shyr & Ou-Yang 2016 PPP 32:5 — confirmed sharp transition at 370 nm; 4-5% UV reflection
Smijs & Pavel 2011 Nanotechnol Sci Appl 4:95 — bandgap 3.22-3.32 eV → λcutoff ~ 370-380 nm

concentration_nonlinearity.model: f(c) = 1 - alpha * tanh(max(0, c - c0) / scale)
concentration_nonlinearity.rationale: Captures aggregation + film-thickness density effect at high ZnO loading. f(0..2%)=1.0, f(20%)=0.36, f(25%)=0.31. Anchored to industry SPF/% benchmark (1.4 to 2.8).
concentration_nonlinearity.source: Fitted to (a) Sunscreen Co 2024 industry analysis 1.4-2.8 SPF/%, (b) Badger/ThinkSport/Aveeno labelled in-vivo SPFs at 20-25% ZnO, (c) Hupel et al. 2024 PPSci on density-induced film-thickness effect

spf_model.formula: SPF = ∫ E_solar(λ) E_ery(λ) dλ / ∫ E_solar(λ) E_ery(λ) 10^(-A(λ)) dλ

caveats: Peak E1%=160 is the dispersed-particle (intrinsic) value at λ_max ~ 350-360 nm. Real cosmetic films show effective k 30-50% lower due to aggregation, captured by f(c).
Range across literature: E1% peak 110-200 (k = 11-20 L/g/cm in Croda patent). Central estimate 160 corresponds to 'preferred' patent values 14-16 L/g/cm.
Spectrum below 290 nm not relevant (solar UVB cutoff at sea level).
Particle-size correction is approximate; 50 nm primary represents Z-COTE-grade ZnO. Pigment-grade (>200 nm) has substantially lower mass-specific k.
Coating effects (silica, dimethicone, triethoxycaprylylsilane) shift k by <10% in UV; included as additional uncertainty band.

SPF model uses CIE 1987 erythema action spectrum and ASTM G173 solar irradiance. Beer-Lambert with concentration nonlinearity; no explicit Mie scattering correction (5% reflection per Cole 2016 is small).
